assessment.construct_summary: All three peer messages convey the intended construct: there is no budget revision provided and the recipient should rely on the currently available evidence. The Vietnamese and Chinese versions are concise imperative directives paralleling the English, with minor tone/register differences (Chinese uses a polite "请"; Vietnamese uses directive particle "Hãy"). Terminology choices are close, with slight naturalness preferences possible (VI: “điều chỉnh” vs “sửa đổi”; ZH: “预算调整/更新” vs “预算修订”, and “现有” vs “可用”).
assessment.limitations: Judgments reflect model-based linguistic assessment, not definitive linguistic truth. Tone/authority in short directives can vary by dialect and register. In Vietnamese, “sửa đổi” vs “điều chỉnh” can be context-sensitive; in Chinese, “修订/调整/更新” and “现有/可用” have subtle nuances. Cultural expectations for politeness vs direct imperatives may vary across regions and domains. These nuances are noted but considered minor for this construct.

As with any brief prompts, subtle connotations of “approved budget update” could vary (e.g., ‘an update to the approved budget’ vs. ‘an update that is approved’), though all three renderings align with the intended construct. Judgments are model-based and not authoritative native-speaker evaluations.

Shared English system context is intentionally unchanged and not treated as localization error.
